key_insight: A quantum interaction graph (QIG) transpilation method lowers routing costs and scales to distributed superconducting quantum architectures with restricted connectivity.
engineering_relevance: Hardware-aware mapping and routing can make compilation more practical for multi-QPU systems without assuming ideal connectivity.
method: Represent circuit interactions using a quantum interaction graph.
Partition the graph to map computations across QPUs.
Apply a fast SABRE-inspired heuristic to route under inter- and intra-module connectivity constraints.
evidence_signal: On a 48-qubit system, QIG reduced average aggregated costs by up to 24.72% and delivered over 250× speed-ups for structured workloads versus DMapS; on 399-qubit IBM Flamingo, it maintained practical runtimes and cut structured routing costs by up to 51.96% versus DQC-adapted SABRE.
watch_item: Reported gains depend on workload, topology, and baseline; the abstract does not establish execution-fidelity improvements on physical hardware.
paper_title: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures
